en: The Thousand-Name Hymn of Śrī Vaṭukabhairava
The Goddess said:
O Lord of Gods, easily accessible through devotion, saluted by the leaders of the gods, please tell me truly the primary cause for the fulfillment of the desires of devotees. (1)
"O Lord, it may come about even without the web of ritual deposits (nyāsa), without worship,
without physical austerity, and even without recitation.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
Of this mantra of the Thousand Names of the Auspicious Vaṭukabhairava, Brahmānandabhairava is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), Vaṭukabhairava is the deity (devatā);
"vaṃ" is the seed-syllable (bīja), "hrīṃ" is the power (śakti), and it is employed in recitation for the sake of attaining the desired fruit.
Vaṭuka, the granter of desires, the Lord, the beloved of the Lord, the maker of light;
Bhairava, the destroyer of fear, pride, Kandarpa, he whose banner is the fish;
Rudra, the youth, the lord of prosperity, the lord of beings, the progenitor of creatures.
The compassionate one, the fierce one, the sovereign, the lord of women, the beloved of the world;
the god, the lord of the Daityas, the hero, the one honored by heroes, the maker of the day;
the favorite of Bali, the best of gods, the youngest, the infant of the youngest.
He is of great strength and great splendor, the conqueror of wealth, the increaser of glory;
he is radiant, heroic, aged, ever-increasing, and the leader of all beings.
He is Time, the transformation of skulls, desires, and the like, and the crusher of lust.
He who delights in desire, the desirous one, the leader, the beloved of Kālikā; 7. the lord of Kālī, the lover of the passionate woman, the increaser of Kālikā’s bliss;
he who knows the heart of Kālikā, the son of Kālikā, the righteous one. 8.
Lord of birds, sky-traveler, celestial body, distinguished, lover of the celestial body;
Kumāra, wrathful, beloved of Kālī, protector of the mountains;
Gaṇejya, enumerator, hidden, one of hidden intent, Lord of the Gaṇas.
Lord of the Gaṇas, foremost of the Gaṇas, chief of the Gaṇas, beloved of the Gaṇas;
10 Lord of the Terrible, dark as a rain-cloud, cloud-bodied, whose nature is the cloud;
destroyer of the terrible, Lord of the clouds, Lord of wealth, whose nature is wealth. 11
Resembling the *campaka* flower, long-lived, beautifully attired, and the mover of both the moving and the unmoving;
he is the final one, possessed of an inconceivable host, wise, abiding in the pure mind, and the Lord of Consciousness (12).
He holds the parasol, is the master of the parasol, and is dear to those whose noses have been severed by the parasol.
He whose radiance is severed, who has severed all affliction, who is the vomit of vomiting, the delighter of those who have vomited;
he is the person, the victorious one, the one with matted hair, the lord, the crusher of men, the lord of men;
he whose abode is in people, the satisfaction of people, and the destroyer of the dullness of people.
He who is the leader of the people, who is propitiated by the people, the overseer of the people, and beloved by the people;
the destroyer of living beings, the giver of life, the creature, the lord of life, and the sovereign of men (15);
the bestower of victory, the conqueror, the victorious, the glory of victory, and the increaser of victory.
The ground of victory, the form of victory, the cause of victory, the lord of victory;
he whose soul is vomited forth from the heart of the sound *jhaṅkāra*, the cause of that sound, the self-born one;
the mistress of the letter *jña* and *bha*, Hari the sustainer, the bearer, the lord of servants. (16–17)

He whose heart is the syllable *ṭhī*, the leader of the eight lords of the *ṭhaṅka* [breaths], adorned with the syllable *ṭha*, the lord of the eighty openings of the body, the master of the eighty lords;
he who is dear to *ḍuḍī* and *ḍakkā*, the traveler, the king of *ḍuṇḍhi*, who is without end. (18)
Tāmra, Tamīśvara, Sreta, Tīrthajāta, Taḍitprabhu;
Ṛkṣara, Ṛkṣakastambha, Tārkṣyaka, Stambhadeśvara;
Sthalaja, Sthāvara, Sthātṛ, Sthirabuddhi, and Sthitendriya.
He whose kinsmen are steadfast, whose affection is steadfast, whose state is steadfast, and whose resolve is steadfast;
He who is fearless, the one whose belly is the abode of the serpent, the deceptive one, and the lover of the pomegranate flower (21);
He who destroys poverty, the divine one, the one with a divine body, and the one with celestial luster.
The performer of initiation, the lord of day, the master of the day, the maker of day;
the one of long peace, the light of the petals, the lord of the petals, the beautiful one of the petals;
the lover of the petals, the splendor of the petals, the best of the petals, the sovereign of the petals.
He whose splendor is like a petal, who has the form of a petal, who is served by petals, and who is honored by petals;
he who possesses the excellence of long arms, whose form is like a leaf, a sprout, and a petal;
the lord of the Dānavas, an ocean of compassion, merciful, and beloved by the distressed.
Lord of wealth, giver of wealth, Dharma, king of wealth, lover of wealth;
bestower of wealth, supervisor of wealth, honored for wealth, conqueror of wealth;
wise, elemental, creator, smoke-colored, and increaser of the hue of smoke.
Dhaniṣṭha, the one who possesses a hundred million treasures, the one who desires wealth, the lord of wealth;
the steadfast one, the most steadfast, the cow, the lord of the stream, the sovereign of the earth.
(27) The protector of the earth, the ruler of the earth, the leader of the earth, the supporter.
The beloved of the earth, the protector of the earth, the sustainer of the earth, the one dear to the earth;
the support of the earth, the one invincible by the earth, the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Lord of Wealth;
Nārada, the man-like, the leader, the one worthy of worship through prostration, the Lord of prostration.
He who is not to be surpassed, the supreme lord, the most light, the sovereign;
the son of Pāṇḍu, the one worshipped by the sons of Pṛthā, the giver of water, the one who is bowed to, the vast one.
The ancient one, the giver of life, the traveler, the princess of Pañcāla, and the lord of fire.
Lord of the earth, son of Pṛthā, sovereign over those who bear the earth; 31 The foremost lord of heroes, the most excellent, the giver of joy, the increaser of joy;
Lord of Pārvatī, supreme ruler, beloved of Pārvatī’s heart. 32
The beloved of Pārvatī, the purified, the purifier, the destroyer of sins; satisfied by a multitude of worthy and unworthy recipients, the perfectly contented, the Supreme Person, the dear one;
the Lord of the full moon, the sovereign of the mountains, the mountain, and the son of the Leader (Nārāyaṇa). || 33 ||
Phālguna, Phalguna, Nātha, Phaṇeśa, Phaṇirakṣaka;
Phaṇīpati, Phaṇīśāna, Phaṇālinda, Phaṇākṛti;
Balabhadra, Balī, Bāla, Baladhī, Balavardhana.
He whose life-force is strength, the lord of strength, the one who makes the offering of Bali dear to him;
the king of Bali, whose life-force is Bali, the master of strength, the sovereign of Bali;
the powerful one, strength itself, the lord of children, the child, and he of pleasing appearance.
The auspicious one, the bestower of auspiciousness, the formidable, Bhīmasena, the inspirer of fear;
the worthy one, the lover of the worthy, the lord of beings, the destroyer of beings;
the lord of beings, the bestower of prosperity, Bharga, the past and future of beings, and the lord of existence.
Bhavānī’s Lord, the Lord of Bhavā, the Leader of Bhavānīs, and Bhava;
the letter Ma, Mādhava, Pride, the Fish-bannered One, and Maheśvara;
the Great Sage, Madana, the Churning-stick, the Lord of the Gemini, and the Sovereign of the Immortals.
Marīci, Mañjula, Moha, Mohahā, Mohamardana;
Mohaka, Mohana, Medhāpriya, Mohavināśaka;
Mahīpati, Maheśāna, Mahārāja, Maheśvara.
Lord of the earth, protector of the earth, master of the earth, beloved of the earth;
sustainer of the earth, sovereign of the earth, king of Madhura, beloved of the sages;
silent, observer of silence, cloud, celestial coral tree, and increaser of the intellect.
He whose intellect is slow, the counsel, the lord of counselors, and the leader of mantras.
(43) The wise, the giver of honor, the proud, the destroyer of pride, and the crusher of arrogance;
he who moves through the fish, the lord of Capricorn, the crocodile, and the invincible jewel. (44)
Delightful as a jewel, brother of jewels, adorned with a circle of jewels;
the secret counsel of the minister, charming, the giver of liberation, beloved of liberation;
the wrestler, dear to wrestlers, the mantra, the uniter, possessing the splendor of union.
He whose delight is the fragrance of jasmine, who possesses the luster of *mālatī* flowers;

the lord of *mālatī*, the sovereign of *maghā*, whose form is *māgha*, the lord of *maghā*; who has the appearance of the root (*mūla*), the destroyer of the root, the root itself, the uprooter, and that which originates from the root.
He who is bewildered by the luster of rubies, the heap of jewels, and the lover of gems;
the deliverer from suffering, the intoxicating one, the gentle, he who is to be saluted by the intoxicated, and the lord of Manu.
(48) He who dwells in the mind, the lord of Menakā, and he whose appearance is dear to Menakā.
Yama, Yāmala, Yetā, Yādava, and the leader of the Yadus (Yadunāyaka);
the beggar (Yācaka), the performer of sacrifice (Yajñaka), the sacrifice (Yajña), the Lord of Sacrifice (Yajñeśa), the Increaser of Sacrifice (Yajñavardhana);
the Lord of Ramā (Ramāpati), the Sovereign of Ramā (Ramādhīśa), the Master of Ramā (Rameśa), and the Beloved of Rāmā (Rāmavallabha).
The Lord of Ramā, the Master of Ramā, the Beloved of Ramā, the Sovereign of Ramā;
the Delighter of Revatī, Rāma, the Lord of Rāmā, the Joy of Rāmā;
the one of beautiful form, the Lord of Rati, the Leader of Rākā, the Sun.
Lakṣmīdhara, Lalajjihva, devoted to the recitation of the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī; Lampaṭa, Lambarājeśa, Lambadeśa, Lakārabhū;
Vāmana, Vallabha, Vandhya, Vanamālī, and Valeśvara.
Established in self-control, forest-dweller, the fruitful, king of the forest, delighter of the forest;
wanderer of the forest, lord of the forest, adorned with a garland of forest flowers.
Beloved of the flute, forest-formed, worthy of praise by the lords of the forest, master of the forest.
Śambhu, the one pleased by Śaṅkara, the enemy of Śambara, the eternal;

he who is saluted by the Śabara woman, the Śāla tree, the one fond of the sound of arrows, the Śakula fish, the porcupine, good character, the cool-rayed moon, and the one clad in white raiment. || 55-56 ||
The giver of virtue, the shower, the virtuous one, the one endowed with virtue, the slow-moving;
the perfected one, the maker of perfection, the goal to be attained, the source of perfection, the one who contemplates perfection;
the beloved of the established conclusions, the ocean, the one who frequents the shores of the ocean.
The lord of the Sindhu, the sovereign of the gods, the lotus-eyed one;
the lord of rivers, residing in the river, the lake, the ocean, and the mountain-lake;
the friend, the heroic one, the charioteer, the conscious one, the lord of the virtuous, and the pure white one.

The King of Rivers, the eternally existent, the ever-auspicious, the goal of the virtuous; he who is like unto himself, the patient one, the hero, the one being served, the husband of the virtuous (Satī);
the Sun, the Lord of the Sun, the one to be served, the lover of service, the eternal.
The lord of Śanī, the protector of Śaśin, served by Satī, delighting in Satī; the life-breath of Satī, the lord of Satī, served by Satī, the sovereign of Satī;
the king of the Siddhas, pleased with Satī, the minister, whose vehicle is on the left.
He who is satisfied with the virtuous leader, Savyasācin, Samantaka, the one accompanied by Citrā, the delight of all, the bestower of success through the propitiation of all,
the one to be propitiated by all, the one addressed by Śacī, the husband of the virtuous woman, and the one well-served. (63)
Sāgara, Sagara, together with Samudra and Priyadarśana;
Samudreśa, the supreme protector, whose eyes are like lotuses;
he who has the form of a cloud over the lake, and who is worshipped by the clouds over the lake.
The knower of bodily marks (sāmudrika), whose very self is the ocean (samudrātman), he who is served by the lords of the gods;
he who is served by the gods, the sovereign lord of the gods, the protector of the gods, and the ruler of the gods.
He is the presiding overseer of the gods, the one to be propitiated by the gods, and the one who is proficient among the multitude of gods.
The best of gods, the life-breath of the gods, the dweller by the celestial river;
the lover of nectar, the lord of nectar, he who is to be won by nectar, the master of nectar;
the protector of nectar, the embodiment of nectar, served by the ocean of nectar.
Hāṭaka, Hīraka, Hantā, Hāṭaka, Ruciraprabha;
Havyavāha, Haridrābha, Haridrārasamardana;
Heti, Hetu, Hari, Nātha, Harinātha, and Haripriya. 69.
Worshipful to Hari, the life-breath of Hari, delighted by Hari, yellow-hued;
lord of monkeys, the slayer of Tripura, the diamond, devoted to the name of Hari;
enchanted by Hari, delightful to Hari, the servant of Hari, the sovereign of monkeys.
The one whose necklace is a garland of sapphire, who steals the hearts of deer, the destroyer (Hara),
the benefactor, whose life-force is Viṣṇu, who is beautiful with the vehicle of the monkey (Hanumān).
He is the swan, the lover of laughter, the utterer of "Huṃ-huṃ," the consumer of oblations, and the one who carries the sacrificial fire.
The consumer of oblations, the one who utters "hik," whose weapon is the *hālāhala* poison;
73 Shaped like a plow, the lord of those with plows, worshipped by those with plows, beloved by those with plows;
the son of Hara, possessing the vigor of Hara, the offspring of Hara, born from Hara. 74
He who is bound by Hara, the lord of Hara, the ender of Hara, and whose form is like Hara;
he who is the life-breath of Hara, who is honored by Hara, and the destroyer of Hara’s enemies (75);
he who is the foe of Hara, worthy of worship by Hara, the syllable *huṃ*, and the beloved of the female deer.
Hāṭakeśa, Hareśāna, Hāṭakapriyadarśana;
Hāṭaka, Hāṭakaprāṇa, Hāṭabhūṣaṇabhūṣaka; Hetida, Hetika, Haṃsa, Haṃsāgatirāhvaya.
The lord of female swans, the intoxicated Hara, the lord of female swans, the beloved of Hara;
he whose splendor is like the flower of Hara, the lover of female swans, who sports with the swan;
he who delights in the life of Hara, the captivating one, the green one, the lord of the quarters.
The Lord of the green [direction], the protector of the green, the leader within the green; the Lord of the green, predominantly green, the benefactor of those dear to Hari.
Heramba, the one who utters "huṃ" with wrath; Heramba, the two who utter "huṃ," the two Haris.
The destroyer of Heramba’s life, the one dear to the heart of Heramba;
the lord of the earth, patient for a moment, sharp as a razor’s edge, the sovereign of the world;
the ruler of the earth, the sustainer of the earth, the diminished one, the protector of the earth, the master of the earth. (81)
Lord of the earth, life-breath of the earth, leader of the earth, beloved of truth;
king of the earth, lord of the moment, master of the moment, sovereign of the moment; lover of the moment, protector of the earth, beloved of the lord of the night. (82–83)
Momentary, the lord of the moment, the giver of life to the night, the patient one;
capable, the lord of the earth, the agitation, the cause of agitation, the lover of forgiveness;
84. of a forgiving nature, the form of forgiveness, adorned by the circle of the earth.
Lord of forbearance, the foundation of forbearance, the upholder of forbearance, the sustainer of forbearance;
85 the one who brings security, the one whose afflictions are diminished, the destroyer of the base, the expert protector of the lowly;
the one seated upon the base, whose form is momentary, and who is intent on the drinking of milk. 86
Lying in milk, lord of the moments, sustainer of the earth, festival of the night;
bringing security, desiring the earth, the ornament of the heart of forgiveness;
possessing a beautiful presence like a blue mountain, resembling a mass of dark clouds.
Delightful with the luster of sapphires, adorned with blue ornaments,
blue in color, and having blue eyebrows; he is decorated with a garland of severed heads,
resides upon severed heads, is satisfied by severed heads, wears a garland of severed heads, and is the embodiment of policy.
Clad in the directions, his form is well-known; he is the bestower of boons to those who wear no clothes.
He is the Lord of the sky-clad, blissful, and the one who delights in binding the quarters.
He has tawny hair tied in a single lock, he is joyful, and he is fond of beating the hand-drum (ḍamaru).
The leader of guilds, the one whose hope lies in the guild, the wielder of the sword, the protector of the sword;
the trident-bearer, resembling an elephant, beautiful with the festival of elephants;
the bestower of fearlessness, the one with curved thighs, the lord of Laṅkā, the leader.
The lord of mountains, adorned with a circle of serpents,
having the form of a serpent, the sovereign of serpents, reclining upon a serpent, and fond of serpents;
the one who emerged from the jar, having the form of a jar, and skilled in sounding the bell.
The Lord who holds a skull in his hand, the autumnal one whose food is a skull;

he who holds a lotus in his hand, whose mouth is formidable, who has three eyes, and who is dear to the serpents; he who rejoices in a network of tinkling bells, the refuge of people, and the leader of mankind.

The remover of untimely death, the destroyer of the root of illusion and delusion; the bestower of long life, the lord of Kamalā, the beloved of the husband of Kamalā. (96) The giver of sovereignty, the sovereign lord of kings, as splendid as a king among kings.
The leader of the ḍākinīs, eternal, devoted to the eternal Dharma;
the knower of the heart-knowledge of the ḍākinīs, the leader of the bodies of the ḍākinīs;
the bestower of life to the ḍākinīs, the accomplished one (siddha), whose conduct is trustworthy, the all-pervading Lord. 97–98.
Hemaprabha, Himeśāna, Himānīpriyadarśana,
Hemada, Narmada, Mānī, Nāmadheya, Nagātmaka;
Vaikuṇṭha, Vāsukiprāṇa, Vāsukīkaṇṭhabhūṣaṇa.
Kuṇḍalīśa, destroyer of the sacrifice, king of sacrifices, lord of sacrifices;
the form of the sacrifice, sovereign of the sacrifice, adorned with a garland of sacrifices;
beloved of Ambikā, whose intellect is speech, and who is proficient in speech.

Lord of speech, whose life-breath is his voice, who abides in words, and who is dear to the forest; the support of the shore, the hope of the quarters, the portion of the directions, and indeed the lord of the directions (102);
beloved by the clever, difficult to propitiate, and capable of shattering poverty.
He who delights in logic and inquiry, the inconceivable one, the object of deliberation, and the beloved of reasoning;
he who is perfected through logic, whose self is perfectly realized, whose body is perfected, and whose seat is the planets;
he who possesses planetary pride, the lord of the planets, the fragrance, the one skilled in the fragrant, and the expert.
Auspiciousness itself, the embodiment of auspiciousness, the player of auspicious musical instruments;
Maṅgalīśa, seated in his celestial chariot, the sole excellent leader of that chariot.
Budheśa, the lord of various sciences, the day of Mercury, and the source of wisdom.
The Lord of the Wise, beloved by the Wise, worthy of homage by the Wise, the Sovereign of the Wise;
accomplished by the Wise, the life-force of the Wise, dear to the Wise, the Knower among the Wise.
Soma, whose form is like the moon, the drinker of Soma, the leader of Soma. 106–107.
Somaprabha, Somasiddha, the leader of mind and vital breath; he who moves at will, the destroyer of desire, the Buddha, the bestower of the fruits of desire, the sovereign;
Tridaśa, the lord of the ten nights, the destroyer of the ten-faced Rāvaṇa.
Lakṣmaṇa, the sustainer of a hundred thousand, he who is numbered among the targets, the beloved of the mind;
Vibhāvasu, the new Īśāna, the leader, the lover of the city;
the ender of Naraka, possessing the energy of Nala, the god among men, having the form of Nara.
Narapati, Nareśāna, Nārāyaṇa, and Nareśvara;
Anila, Māruta, Māsa, and he who is devoted to the singular essence of flesh (Māṃsaikarasasevita);
Marīci, Amareśāna, Māgadha, and Magadhaprabhu.
Sundarīsevaka, Dvārī, and Dvāradeśanivāsina;
Devakogarbhajāta, Devakīsevaka, and Kuhu; Bṛhaspati, Kavi, Śukra, and Śāradāsādhanapriya. 112–113.
His life-breath was for the practitioner of Śāradā, he was eager to serve Śāradā, and he was the most excellent of Śāradā’s practitioners; his constant delight was in drinking wine.
He took pleasure in receiving sweetmeats and was gladdened by the fragrance of those sweetmeats.
Āmodānandana, Nanda, Nandikeśa, Maheśvara;
Nandipriya, Nadīnātha, and likewise Nadītīrataru;
Tapana, Tāpana, Tapta, Tāpahā, and Tāpakāraka. (115–116)
Pataṅgagomukha, Gauragopāla, Gopavardhana;
Gopati, Gopasaṃhartā, Govindaikapriya, Atiga;
Gavyeṣṭha, Gaṇaramya, Guṇasindhu, and Guṇapriya. || 117 ||
Worthy of worship for his virtues, endowed with virtues, a proclaimer of virtues, and a festival of virtues;
the sole essence of the virtuous, the womb, the excellent womb, and the protector of the womb;
the upholder of profundity, the sustainer, the ordainer, and the guardian of Dharma.
Lord of the world, friend of the world, destroyer of the dullness of elephants;
creator of the world, sustainer of the world, the very life of the life of the world.
Delighted by the *mālatī* flower, he for whom the *mālatī* blossom is a festival.
Having the form of a *mālatī* flower, possessing the luster of a *mālatī* flower;
delightful with clusters of mango blossoms, perfumed by the scent of mangoes;
longing for mango clusters, he is the beloved of the mango tree. (121–122)
Seated beneath the *rasāla* tree, beautiful with the fruit of the *rasāla*,
satisfied by the essence of the *rasāla*, and taking refuge in the juice of the *rasāla*; satisfied by the *ketakī* flower, he is born from the heart of the *ketakī*.
Resembling the leaf of the *ketakī* flower, yet the destroyer of the *ketakī*'s life;
dwelling in a pit, as deep as a pit, and residing on the banks of a pit;
served by the hosts, the leader of the hosts, the king of the hosts, and named after the hosts.
Ānandabhairava, Bhīru, Bhairaveśa, Ruru, Bhaga, Subrahmabhairava, Nāmabhairava, and Bhūtabhāvana;
the son of Bhairavī, the son of the Goddess, who resembles a mountain.

Having praised Vaṭukabhairava with these one thousand names, one indeed attains incomparable prosperity, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain. Having received the instruction from the Guru, one becomes a member of the circle of the lords of yoga.
In that yoga, the Great Lord shall attain all perfections;
the practitioner of mantra, a lord among men, by reciting the king of mantras one hundred thousand times,
will certainly obtain the fruit thereof for the sake of success in his daily rites.
Having recited this hymn according to the prescribed rite,
the practitioner of mantra attains the rare accomplishment honored by all the gods.
This must never be disclosed to one's son, nor ever to those who have fallen from their vows.
Otherwise, there would be an obstruction to success, or he might become dear to the four [castes].
By his grace, he shall be as beloved as the gods;
in battle, he shall conquer his enemies like a lion conquers elephants.
It shall instantly bring kings under one's control and even lead the gods to tranquility.
What further fruit could be described as obtained from this King of Hymns? Whatever desire is conceived in the mind, this hymn, when recited, [fulfills it]. (133–134)
O Lord of Gods, by the grace of Vaṭuka, one attains each and every such thing;
for it is the cause for the destruction of calamities, difficult even for beloveds to obtain, and a benefactor to the gods in the terrible battle between the gods and asuras. (135)
O Lord, this has been revealed by me in the *Bhairavadīpaka Tantra*.
By reciting or causing others to recite this unsurpassed king of hymns, even one who is childless shall obtain sons within six months, provided it is done continuously. (136–137)
The poor man obtains wealth, and one attains a very long life;
the seeker of a daughter obtains a daughter endowed with every beauty.
By offering oblations at twilight, one may bring the entire world under one's control.

One should constantly recite [the mantra] while observing a banyan tree, the root of a *bilva* tree, a plantain tree, or in a forest grove, for the sake of attaining mastery over the King of Mantras. Alternatively, one may recite it one hundred thousand times; indeed, this has been shown merely as a general indication. (139–140)
One should worship with sesame seeds, black gram, milk, meat, and jhava fish;
or else with ghee-cooked rice and side dishes abounding in savory flavors.
A true practitioner should either perform such worship or maintain this hymn.
O beloved of the gods, for those who recite this or cause it to be recited according to the prescribed rite, there shall be no fear from enemies, nor fear arising from fire, thieves, or weapons;
nor even any fear arising from fever and the like—this is the truth, the absolute truth, O Maheśvarī! (142–143)
"O Lord, that practitioner who becomes capable of worshipping Bhairava should be known as Sadāśiva himself; so it has been declared by Bhairava.
For a person who has entered the practice of serving the glorious King Bhairava, there arise the fivefold, the ninefold, and indeed the eight great supernatural powers (mahāsiddhis). (144)

"May the gods, who are the garlands of light from the crest-jewels at the tips of the crowns of the protectors of the earth, pour water upon the head of him who bears the majesty of your terrestrial fame upon his lotus-feet.
(145) Thus ends the *Śrī-vaṭukabhairava-sahasranāmastotra*, in the dialogue between the Goddess and Hara within the *Bhairavatantra*. It is complete.
